customer.business: Skill-hire: a marketplace to hire specialized AI agents (base model + one open-source Agent Skill) as named AI workers
customer.target: People and teams who pay for digital work today (freelancers, software, or their own time) and might hire an AI worker instead

segments.name: Small-business owner who buys on Fiverr/Upwork
In-house developer already using Claude Code/Cursor

behaviours.name: Tinkerer
behaviours.how: Would rather install the free skill and run it themselves than pay a middleman.

behaviours.name: Outcome buyer
behaviours.how: Pays for finished work, does not care how it is made, judges only results.

behaviours.name: Burned before
behaviours.how: Has tried GPT Store bots or AI agents that over-promised; skeptical by default.

behaviours.name: Loyal to a platform
behaviours.how: Lives in one tool (Claude, ChatGPT, Upwork) and buys what it offers.

behaviours.name: Procurement-gated
behaviours.how: Needs security review, SOC 2, DPA and a vendor contract before any spend.

behaviours.name: Deal hunter
behaviours.how: Tries free tiers, cancels subscriptions fast, compares price per result.

objections: The skills are free and open-source, why would I pay you to run one?
Claude/ChatGPT already does this with skills built in
I don't trust a third party with my repo, files and credentials
AI output still needs a human to check it, so I'm paying twice
Who is liable when the agent gets it wrong?
I tried the GPT Store and every bot was a thin wrapper
A freelancer on Fiverr is cheap and I can talk to them
habits: you already pay $20-200/month for an AI subscription
you posted a job on Upwork or Fiverr in the last 3 months
you ship code daily and have a stack of half-finished side projects
you have a vendor review backlog of 40+ AI tools
you bill clients by the project and margins are getting squeezed by AI

pitch:
Skill-hire: browse a catalog of specialist AI workers (UI/UX designer, Excel analyst, security auditor, copywriter...). Each is a frontier model plus one tested open-source Agent Skill, run on our platform.
Hire one, connect your files, repo or tools, and get finished work back, usually within the hour.
Price: pay per task from $9 to $99 depending on the job, or $49/month per worker for unlimited small tasks. First task free.
Skill authors list workers and get a revenue share. Early-stage startup; no SOC 2 yet.
